facts.text: Beazer's USD 250.0 million 7.5% notes due 2031 and USD 400.0 million 8.0% notes due 2032 were assumed at closing. On 22 October 2026 Dream Finders offered new notes of its own with the same interest, maturity and redemption terms in exchange, with a consent solicitation to remove substantially all restrictive covenants and events of default from the Beazer indentures. Holders of 98.64% of the principal had tendered by 4 November 2026; for each USD 1,000 tendered by that date they receive USD 1,000 of new notes and USD 1.00 in cash, and later tenders receive USD 950 of new notes. The offers expire on 20 November 2026 unless extended, and settlement is expected on 23 November 2026, after the as-of date. The guarantors, ranking and covenants of the new notes are not stated in the documents supplied. facts.label: T2D.9 - Sponsor and governance risk assessment
facts.text: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by founder control with pledged shares and by a large debt-funded acquisition, because both raise event and leverage risk for creditors, which implies close monitoring rather than a restrictive view. Countervailing evidence is the absence of common dividends, of fees to the controlling holder beyond the aircraft lease and of any action against existing noteholders. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the margin loan terms and pro forma debt. Basis: calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C14

facts.text: Dream Finders builds single-family homes for entry-level, move-up and active adult buyers in the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, sells homes to rental investors under built-for-rent contracts and earns mortgage, title and insurance income from the same buyers; it acquired Beazer on 20 October 2026. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: The company is founder-led and publicly listed with no sponsor. The founder holds all Class B stock, about 84% of the votes, and the company is a controlled company that could opt out of independent-board requirements; part of his stake is pledged for margin loans and the new Series B stock gives holders a cash redemption right if his holding falls below 50% of votes or economic interest. The parent is a holding company that depends on its operating subsidiaries, whose guarantors are not named, and the preferred stock ranks ahead of common stock but is classified as mezzanine equity, so creditors rely on the operating subsidiaries' cash flow and a stable control position. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C15

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue depends on volume, price and mix, and is cyclical and discretionary. In nine months closings rose 1% while the average selling price fell 7.71%, driven by geographic and product mix and more built-for-rent closings, and net sales rose 6% with the help of incentives and mortgage buydowns, with a cancellation rate of 10.2% against 12.7%. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Costs are mostly variable but the largest items are rising. Homesite costs are typically 30% to 35% of a home's cost, materials 30% to 35%, labor 20% to 25% and interest, commissions and closing costs 5% to 10%, and the company reports higher land and financing costs as the main cause of lower margin. Direct cost cuts and cycle-time gains have not offset a 3.2 percentage point fall in homebuilding gross margin, and homebuilding SG&A rose to 12.5% of revenue from 12.0%, so margins are not defended under price pressure; the company can cut compensation and terminate land options, which provides partial flexibility. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 45; Business & governance (CP-1A)

facts.text: Capital expenditure is small, but inventory is the capital need and it is growing. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense and barriers to entry are low: the company competes with larger national builders and smaller local builders, and builders are using pricing adjustments, mortgage buydowns and incentives to hold sales, which presses margin and cash flow. Substitutes are resale homes and rentals, and rising resale inventory gives buyers alternatives, while buyers are highly payment sensitive. Land developers and land bank partners hold supply-side power over lot terms and fees, and trades and materials suppliers can pass on price and labor pressure, so the main credit effect is margin and cash-flow durability rather than market share. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 7

facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Macro and policy factors are material because they move demand and cost together. Mortgage rates rose late in the third quarter, consumer confidence weakened to near-record lows, and management expects higher energy, materials and labor costs and tighter skilled labor availability, including from changes in immigration enforcement. Each pushes down closings or margin at the same time as debt rises, so they bear directly on interest cover and liquidity; technology and social factors are not a primary credit driver on the documents supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 32

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the near-term headwinds are weak affordability, sustained incentives, higher land and financing costs, the integration of Beazer, expected deal abandonment charges in the fourth quarter and the 2027 commitments maturity; the tailwinds are cost reductions already under way, shorter cycle times and a backlog made up mostly of spec homes that close quickly. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario starts with mortgage rates staying high through the fourth quarter, so closings miss the guidance and incentives rise. The first operating break is homebuilding gross margin: a further 3.2 percentage point fall, the same as the fall between the first nine months of 2025 and 2026, takes last-twelve-months EBITDA from USD 373.312 million to USD 247.068 million, lifting net leverage to 7.08x and cutting EBITDA cover of cash interest to 0.81x on pre-closing debt. Financially, operating cash outflow continues while inventory is carried, so borrowing on the Credit Agreement rises toward its borrowing base and liquidity falls below the pre-closing runway of 15.42 months; the Series B dividend of USD 20.25 million a quarter could be deferred, which compounds the claim at 12.0%. Management levers are terminating land options, cutting overhead and slowing starts. On pre-closing figures liquidity would cover about 15.42 months of the outflow, so distress in 2027 is not indicated, but the post-closing position that decides it is not established, and resilience depends on refinancing the August 2028 cluster. The observable triggers are fourth-quarter closings, gross margin, liquidity after closing and any sale of pledged founder shares. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C13

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Dream Finders presents an adequate business profile supported by an asset-light land model, regional breadth and integrated financial services, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 4.69x, interest cover of 1.23x, negative free cash flow and compressed margins before a large acquisition. Cash-flow durability appears weak because inventory growth absorbs earnings. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on housing demand and on market access in 2027 and 2028, when USD 300.0 million of commitments and then 60.07% to 75.10% of pre-closing debt mature. The primary downside path is a further fall in homebuilding gross margin on a larger debt and preferred stock base. Further analysis would require the closing balance sheet, the Credit Agreement drawing, covenant definitions and Beazer's earnings. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: refinancing the August 2028 maturities after margin compression and a debt-funded acquisition. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C6; calculation C8; calculation C13

Action: Obtain any rating action and bond quotes. - Quantitative thresholds for monitoring are the issuer's latest reported levels, not covenant or rating thresholds, because none is supplied. Severity: Low. Action: Replace with covenant levels when the executed documents are available.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt reached 4.69x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 30 September 2026, up from 1.61x at the end of 2024, and EBITDA covered cash interest paid only 1.23x, which leaves creditors little cushion before the Beazer acquisition adds further debt.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C10

The issuer's EBITDA adds back interest charged to homebuilding cost of sales, which makes up 56.15% of last-twelve-months EBITDA against 29.75% for 2024, so these ratios depend on that definition and a lender who excludes the add-back sees much weaker coverage.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C12; calculation C13

Pro forma net debt for the Beazer acquisition that closed on 20 October 2026 is not established: the sources give USD 435.3 million of Series B preferred proceeds and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds, but not the Credit Agreement drawing at closing, Beazer's cash or how the land bank funding is recorded.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_ex991closingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2
The maturity ladder is also not established, because the sources give no maturity dates for the warehouse lines or other borrowings and do not split the revolver drawings between its two tranches.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, pages 9–13

- The maturity ladder is not established: the sources give no maturity dates for the mortgage warehouse lines or other borrowings and do not split the revolver drawings between the tranches maturing on 2027-06-04 and 2028-08-21, so every maturity cell and the contractual principal are shown as not supplied. Severity: High. Action: obtain the warehouse terms and the drawn amount by tranche from the executed credit agreement.

- Pro forma net debt and net leverage after the Beazer acquisition are not established: the sources do not state the Credit Agreement drawing at closing, Beazer's cash and debt at closing, or whether the USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds is recorded as debt or a sale, so the post-balance-sheet rows give amounts only where the sources state them. Severity: High. Action: obtain the closing-date balance sheet or pro forma statements.

- Covenant levels after the amendments of 2026-07-02 and 2026-09-22 are not established: the executed agreement is not supplied and the 2025 annual report states the five tests only as at 2025-12-31. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the executed amendments.

- No adjusted EBITDA is stated by the issuer, so the adjusted EBITDA row, the adjusted ratios and the EBITDA bridge are shown as not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: none needed unless the issuer begins to state one.

- Other borrowings of USD 38.706 million at 2026-09-30 are not itemised: their security, ranking, rate and maturity are not stated and only USD 23.394 million is identified as secured, so this row is left out of the debt stack and its principal is not supplied. - Cash paid for interest is one printed figure with no split between interest capitalized into inventory and interest expensed, and the filings do not say whether it includes lot option fees; the cover ratios use it as printed. Severity: Medium. Action: ask the issuer for the split.

Severity: High. Action: read every leverage and cover figure beside the EBITDA before the add-back.

- The 2025-09-30 balance sheet is only partly printed, with total debt, cash, mezzanine equity and equity but not total assets or total liabilities, so there is no 9M 2025 balance sheet column and no 2025-09-30 leverage ratio. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the third-quarter 2025 quarterly report if that date is needed.

- Lines printed as dashes are shown as not supplied and never as zero: contingent consideration in 9M 2026, the 2024 interest expense in the EBITDA reconciliation, payments for acquisitions in 9M 2026, deposits on pending acquisitions after 2024, investment securities in 2024, senior note proceeds in 2024 and 9M 2026, and the other nil financing lines; the totals add without them. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- Lines printed only in the interim statements (gains on equity securities, preferred stock issuance and redemption, and borrowings related to consolidated inventory not owned) are not supplied for the annual columns, and the contingent consideration line is not printed on the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. Severity: Low. Action: none.
- Capital expenditure is printed only as one line, so no split between maintenance and growth is supplied. Severity: Low. Action: none.
- The fourth quarter of 2025 is not printed and is derived as the fiscal year less nine months; it is labelled calculated and replaces no reported period. Severity: Low. Action: none.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Dream Finders is a founder-controlled, asset-light homebuilder whose USD 2.2 billion Beazer acquisition adds debt, 12.0% preferred stock and land bank funding while margins fall, and governance gives creditors little independent restraint. The founder holds about 84% of the votes and had pledged 61.50% of his Class B stock for margin loans at the end of 2025, against 30.32% a year earlier, and a fall below 50% of votes or economic interest would let Series B holders demand cash.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C11

Offsetting this, the land model limits owned land, no common dividend has ever been paid and the board added homebuilding leadership in 2026, so governance risk is medium rather than high; pro forma debt and liquidity are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 30
### Key findings

Control is concentrated in one person and part of it is financed by pledged shares, so a market-driven forced sale is the main route by which control could change. The founder holds all Class B stock and about 84% of the votes. The share of his Class B stock pledged for margin loans rose from 30.32% at the end of 2024 to 61.50% at the end of 2025, and a further 5.20% was under prepaid forward sale contracts. The lender, loan size and trigger prices are not disclosed. On a simple count of common shares he could part with about 21.58% of his Class B stock before his holding fell to 50% of common shares outstanding, which is well below the share pledged.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2024-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7

The Series B preferred stock ties the founder's holding to a cash claim on the company. Holders can require redemption in cash at the greater of the as-converted value and the liquidation preference, plus accrued dividends, if the founder ceases to own at least 50% of both the voting power and the economic interest, or on a change of control. The face value is USD 675.0 million and the 12.0% cumulative dividend is USD 81.0 million a year, against USD 13.5 million a year on the redeemed 9% Series A stock. The company may defer dividends, which protects cash but compounds the claim at 12.0%. The stock is classified as mezzanine equity and ranks ahead of common stock.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 68; calculation C9; calculation C11; calculation C12

Board independence is not established, and the exemptions open to a controlled company remain available. The company is a controlled company under exchange rules and may opt out of independent-majority and committee requirements; it says it has not used the exemptions at this time. A Co-Chairman with long homebuilding experience and an independent director joined the board in July 2026 and a chief operating officer started in June 2026, which strengthens operating oversight, but the founder remains chief executive and the other Co-Chairman. Which directors are independent is not stated in the documents supplied. The company also reincorporated in Texas on 9 June 2026, and the effect on stockholder and creditor protections is not stated.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_pr-appointmentofbeckwitt-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_dfh-q22026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2

Related-party dealings look modest, but the supply of lots leans on related funds. The company leased an aircraft from a company the founder owns at a cost of USD 4.6 million in 2025. It owns 49.0% of the manager of the land bank funds that supply lots, and officers invest in those funds. Lot deposits with the two related funds were USD 61.6 million at 30 September 2026, 12.57% of all lot deposits, and the company and key executives have committed USD 57.6 million to the newest fund, of which 55.9% has been funded. How the funds' lot terms compare with third-party terms is not disclosed, so pricing leakage cannot be tested.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is structural. The company has never paid a common dividend and the option model keeps owned land low. The insider trading policy was tightened between 2024 and 2025 so that pledges now need board approval without the requesting person's vote. The Series B stock lets the company defer dividends to protect cash. Management states the purchase price was an implied 0.8x of Beazer's book value and expects over USD 100 million of annual run-rate cost synergies, and net sales were a record for the first nine months of 2026.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Dream Finders acquired Beazer Homes USA, Inc. in an all-cash merger signed on 6 August 2026 and completed on 20 October 2026, 75 days later, at USD 33.50 per Beazer share and an enterprise value of about USD 2.2 billion. The offer history published on 11 May 2026 ran from USD 28.50 per share on 5 February to USD 29.00 on 17 March and USD 25.75 on 5 May, so the agreed price is 30.10% above the last of these; management puts the price at an implied 0.8x of Beazer's book value. Management calls it the ninth acquisition since the 2021 listing and by far the largest, and it adds California, Nevada, Indiana and Delaware to the footprint.

- Margin loan lenders, balances and trigger prices are not disclosed, and pledged shares after 2025-12-31 are not stated. Severity: High. Action: Ask the issuer for lenders, loan balances, trigger prices and the current pledged share count.

- The certificate of designations, the investor rights agreement and the names of the Series B purchasers are not supplied, so the definition of economic interest and any governance rights are not established. Severity: High. Action: Obtain the certificate of designations and the investor rights agreement.

- Pro forma debt, liquidity and covenant headroom after the Beazer closing are not established because the amount drawn under the Credit Agreement, Beazer's cash at closing and the debt treatment of the land bank facility are not stated. Severity: High. Action: Wait for the fourth quarter report or ask the issuer for a closing balance sheet.

- Beazer's accounts, the closing balance sheet and the purchase price allocation are not supplied; the quarterly report says the allocation will first appear in the 2026 annual report. Severity: High. Action: Obtain Beazer's last accounts and the preliminary allocation promised in the 2026 annual report.
- The terms of the land bank facility with Millrose and its accounting treatment are not stated. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the land bank agreement and the issuer's accounting for it.

- The guarantors, ranking and covenants of the new notes to be issued in the exchange are not stated because the offering memorandum is not supplied. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the offering memorandum dated 2026-10-22.

- The guarantor subsidiaries of the senior notes and the Credit Agreement are described only as certain subsidiaries and are not named. Severity: Medium. Action: Obtain the guarantor list from the indentures and the Credit Agreement.

- How lot terms with the related land bank funds compare with third-party terms, and the company's own share of the newest fund's commitments, are not disclosed. Severity: Medium. Action: Ask the issuer for the pricing basis of lots bought from related funds.

- How the founder's September 2025 sports franchise interests are funded, and whether the company guarantees or supports them, is not stated. Severity: Low. Action: Ask whether the company guarantees or funds any founder commitment.
- Built-for-rent closings and revenue are not stated as amounts, and no customer concentration is given. Severity: Low. Action: Ask for built-for-rent closings and revenue by period.
- No credit rating or bond price is in the documents supplied. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain any rating action and bond prices.
- Executive employment agreements and compensation terms are not supplied, so incentive alignment is not assessed. Severity: Low. Action: Obtain the employment agreements listed as exhibits.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Dream Finders has a weak and weakening credit profile: net leverage reached 4.69x and interest cover 1.23x before the Beazer acquisition, cash is consumed in every period, and creditors depend on a housing recovery and on refinancing in August 2028. Pro forma net leverage after the closing on 20 October 2026 is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C6; calculation C8

The business is adequate rather than weak: the asset-light land model, three regional segments and record closings give volume, but homebuilding gross margin fell from 17.7% to 14.5% and total liquidity fell 42.03% in nine months, so a deal funded with debt, 12.0% preferred stock and land bank proceeds raises the stakes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C13
### Key findings

Leverage is high and rose fast, and the issuer's own EBITDA flatters it. Net debt of USD 1,750.37 million was 4.69x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 30 September 2026, against 1.61x at the end of 2024, and EBITDA covered cash interest paid only 1.23x; pro forma net debt for the Beazer acquisition of 20 October 2026 is not established. The issuer's EBITDA adds back interest charged to cost of sales, which is 56.15% of the last-twelve-months figure, and without that add-back net debt would be 10.69x EBITDA, so a lender using a stricter definition sees a much weaker position.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation C3; calculation C6

The business does not yet turn earnings into free cash flow, so growth is funded with debt. Operating cash flow was negative in every period reported, and after capital expenditure free cash flow was negative by USD 281,993 thousand in 2024, USD 126,366 thousand in 2025 and USD 320,552 thousand in the first nine months of 2026. Inventory purchases in nine months were 52.51% larger than a year earlier, and negative free cash flow explains 84.59% of the rise in net debt, rising to 97.47% with buybacks and preferred dividends.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4

Earnings are falling faster than revenue because margin is compressing. Revenue fell 5.24% in nine months but EBITDA fell 33.68% and pre-tax income fell 66.59%, homebuilding gross margin was 14.5% against 17.7%, the average selling price fell 7.71% and backlog value fell 8.72%. Management has cut compensation costs and can drop land options, but the cuts have not offset higher land and financing costs, and each percentage point of homebuilding gross margin is worth 10.57% of last-twelve-months EBITDA.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C5; calculation C13; calculation C15

Liquidity was thin before the acquisition closed, and its level after closing is not established. Total liquidity, cash plus revolver availability, fell 42.03% from the end of 2025 to 30 September 2026 and covered 15.42 months at the nine-month rate of operating cash outflow before the acquisition closed. Availability under the Credit Agreement is set by a borrowing base rather than by its commitments, and the amount drawn at closing is not stated.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 73; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C7

Refinancing risk is concentrated in August 2028 and starts earlier. USD 300.0 million of Credit Agreement commitments mature on 4 June 2027, and the commitments of USD 1,200.0 million and the senior notes of USD 300.0 million fall due within a week of each other in August 2028, about 21 months after the as-of date. From the stated commitments, USD 1,199.0 million to USD 1,499.0 million of debt, 60.07% to 75.10% of total debt before the acquisition, matures in that week; this is an analyst bound because the split of drawings between tranches is not stated. Market access is shown but costly: the company raised USD 652.4 million of net Series B proceeds and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds in September and October 2026, at a 12.0% preferred dividend and by trading land for option rights.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 74; calculation C8

The Beazer acquisition raises fixed charges before it adds earnings, and its net effect on leverage is not established. The assumed Beazer notes carry USD 50.75 million of annual coupon and the Series B stock a 12.0% dividend of USD 81.0 million a year, together USD 131.75 million, equal to 35.29% of last-twelve-months EBITDA and 43.30% of last-twelve-months cash interest, before any change in earnings. The enterprise value is 52.38% of pre-closing total assets. Management targets over USD 100 million of annual cost synergies, equal to 26.79% of the same EBITDA, and a return to current leverage metrics within 18 to 24 months, but gives no figure.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_ex991closingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C14

Financial policy is a mixed signal, with no common dividend but concentrated control and pledged shares that add event risk. The founder holds about 84% of the votes, 61.50% of his Class B stock was pledged at the end of 2025 against 30.32% a year earlier, and Series B holders can demand cash if his holding falls below 50% of votes or economic interest. Business & governance rates governance risk medium, and this module agrees because the pledge is an event risk rather than a cash drain on the company today.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C15

The nearest test is the fourth quarter, and the guidance looks demanding. The full-year closings guidance needs a fourth quarter 23.15% above the fourth quarter of 2025 and 1.59x the third quarter of 2026, against 1.32x a year earlier, and backlog homes due in 2026 cover only 48.96% of the closings required. A miss would lower earnings into a larger debt base while the acquisition adds fixed charges.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C9
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weak view is flexibility and access to capital. The asset-light model lets the company drop land options and caps its loss on them at deposits and fees, closings and net sales were records for the period, and the company raised USD 652.4 million of net preferred proceeds and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds in a weak market. Management says the purchase price was an implied 0.8x of Beazer's book value and targets over USD 100 million of annual cost synergies, and the Credit Agreement temporarily allows debt to capitalization of 65.0% instead of 60.0% after a material acquisition.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 30; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C15

The view would improve if pro forma debt and liquidity showed leverage near the pre-closing level, if operating cash flow turned positive as inventory is sold, if homebuilding gross margin held above 14.5% and if the 2027 commitments were extended. It would worsen if fourth-quarter closings missed the guidance, if gross margin fell again by 3.2 percentage points, which would lift net leverage to 7.08x and cut cover to 0.81x before closing, if liquidity after closing proved thinner than the 15.42 months of pre-closing runway, or if pledged founder shares were sold.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C13
### Limitations

- The covenant definitions of debt to capitalization and tangible net worth are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and the leverage conclusion rests on the issuer's own ratios, which could look better or worse against the covenant's own terms.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 74; calculation C12

- The 2028 maturity bounds use commitments that the documents round to the nearest tenth of a billion dollars and drawings at 30 September 2026, so the concentration could be lower if later borrowing sits in the 2027 tranche and higher once closing drawings are added.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C8

- Pro forma leverage, liquidity and cover are not established, so every ratio in this assessment is for the group before the acquisition; the conclusion that the profile is weakening holds on those figures, but its depth after closing could differ.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C7

- Operating cash flow is printed as one line and interest paid is not split between amounts capitalized and expensed, so the cash conversion finding is an arithmetic bridge rather than a measured conversion.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4
- The downside path is built from reported figures and management guidance, and no forecast or stress model was run, so the scale of the sensitivity is indicative and not a prediction.
Basis: calculation C9; calculation C13
### Strengths and weaknesses

- Strength: Asset-light land supply limits capital tied up in land. Option contracts cap the loss on land at deposits and fees, with USD 808 million at risk at 30 September 2026, and let the company terminate options that miss its return thresholds, which gives it a lever to cut spending if demand weakens.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 43; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Strength: Scale and regional breadth spread the demand risk. No homebuilding segment is more than 35.60% of nine-month revenue, closings were a record for the period, and the acquisition adds new states, which softens a local downturn.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_ex991closingpr-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

- Strength: Integrated financial services add a second earnings stream. Mortgage capture was 81.1% in nine months and financial services were 5.47% of revenue, which supports closings and diversifies income, though it is small against the debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 49; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Strength: Access to capital has held in a weak market. The company raised USD 652.4 million of net Series B proceeds and USD 572.1 million of land bank proceeds, which funded part of the acquisition, and it has paid no common dividend.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C15

- Weakness: Leverage and cover are weak and weakening. Net debt was 4.69x last-twelve-months EBITDA and EBITDA covered cash interest 1.23x before the acquisition, which leaves little room for an earnings fall, and pro forma figures are not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6

- Weakness: Free cash flow is negative and debt funds the gap. Free cash flow was negative by USD 320,552 thousand in nine months, with inventory purchases 52.51% larger, so growth adds debt instead of cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3
- Weakness: Margin and order book are shrinking. Gross margin fell to 14.5% from 17.7% and backlog value fell 8.72%, so earnings per home and forward revenue are both lower.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C5; calculation C15

- Weakness: Refinancing is concentrated in August 2028. Between 60.07% and 75.10% of pre-closing debt falls due in one week, after USD 300.0 million of commitments mature in June 2027, so the company depends on market access in 2027 and 2028.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C8

- Weakness: Founder control, pledged shares and a senior preferred claim add event risk. 61.50% of the founder's Class B stock was pledged at the end of 2025, and a fall in his holding below 50% of votes or economic interest lets Series B holders demand cash.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15

### Company description

Dream Finders builds single-family homes for entry-level, move-up and active adult buyers in the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, sells homes to rental investors under built-for-rent contracts and earns mortgage, title and insurance income from the same buyers; it acquired Beazer on 20 October 2026. Revenue is transactional, earned as each home closes, and the order book is mostly spec homes, so cash flow follows closings, mortgage rates and incentives rather than contracts, which weakens visibility for debt service. Financial services are a small second stream and homebuilding dominates earnings.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48
### Ownership and group structure

The company is founder-led and publicly listed with no sponsor. The founder holds all Class B stock, about 84% of the votes, and the company is a controlled company that could opt out of independent-board requirements; part of his stake is pledged for margin loans and the new Series B stock gives holders a cash redemption right if his holding falls below 50% of votes or economic interest. The parent is a holding company that depends on its operating subsidiaries, whose guarantors are not named, and the preferred stock ranks ahead of common stock but is classified as mezzanine equity, so creditors rely on the operating subsidiaries' cash flow and a stable control position.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C15
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue depends on volume, price and mix, and is cyclical and discretionary. In nine months closings rose 1% while the average selling price fell 7.71%, driven by geographic and product mix and more built-for-rent closings, and net sales rose 6% with the help of incentives and mortgage buydowns, with a cancellation rate of 10.2% against 12.7%. Pricing power is weak: management says affordability is acute for entry-level buyers and incentives press on price and margin, and backlog value fell 8.72%, so forward revenue visibility is lower even though closings are at a record for the period.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 48; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C15
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are mostly variable but the largest items are rising. Homesite costs are typically 30% to 35% of a home's cost, materials 30% to 35%, labor 20% to 25% and interest, commissions and closing costs 5% to 10%, and the company reports higher land and financing costs as the main cause of lower margin. Direct cost cuts and cycle-time gains have not offset a 3.2 percentage point fall in homebuilding gross margin, and homebuilding SG&A rose to 12.5% of revenue from 12.0%, so margins are not defended under price pressure; the company can cut compensation and terminate land options, which provides partial flexibility.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 45; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital expenditure is small, but inventory is the capital need and it is growing. Purchases of property and equipment were USD 16,220 thousand in nine months, while inventories rose 24.19% in the balance sheet since year end and used more cash than a year earlier. In nine months EBITDA less cash interest and cash taxes was negative USD 20.573 million before working capital, and operating cash flow was lower still, so EBITDA does not translate into free cash flow available for debt service or deleveraging while the company grows its inventory and lot position.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense and barriers to entry are low: the company competes with larger national builders and smaller local builders, and builders are using pricing adjustments, mortgage buydowns and incentives to hold sales, which presses margin and cash flow. Substitutes are resale homes and rentals, and rising resale inventory gives buyers alternatives, while buyers are highly payment sensitive. Land developers and land bank partners hold supply-side power over lot terms and fees, and trades and materials suppliers can pass on price and labor pressure, so the main credit effect is margin and cash-flow durability rather than market share.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 7
### Macro and policy factors

Macro and policy factors are material because they move demand and cost together. Mortgage rates rose late in the third quarter, consumer confidence weakened to near-record lows, and management expects higher energy, materials and labor costs and tighter skilled labor availability, including from changes in immigration enforcement. Each pushes down closings or margin at the same time as debt rises, so they bear directly on interest cover and liquidity; technology and social factors are not a primary credit driver on the documents supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 32
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths: asset-light land supply with losses capped at deposits and fees; scale across three regions after a ninth acquisition; integrated mortgage and title services; and demonstrated access to preferred and land bank capital. Weaknesses: net leverage of 4.69x before the acquisition, interest cover of 1.23x, negative free cash flow and compressed margins.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6; calculation C1

Opportunities that could improve credit quality: over USD 100 million of targeted annual cost synergies, lower unit costs from scale, and a margin recovery if mortgage rates ease. Threats that could weaken it: weak affordability, a miss against the full-year closings guidance, a forced sale of pledged founder shares, and the refinancing cluster in August 2028.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_dfh_ex-991pressreleasexmergera-htm.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C11
### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is weak on leverage, cover, cash flow and margin, adequate on scale and diversification and not assessable on pro forma liquidity or covenant headroom. The trend is down on every measure between the end of 2024 and 30 September 2026: net leverage rose from 1.61x to 4.69x, cover fell from 3.16x to 1.23x, EBITDA fell 40.72% against 2024 and liquidity fell 42.03% in nine months. The missing datapoints are the post-closing balance sheet and liquidity, covenant definitions and Credit Agreement drawing, the tranche split of drawings, and Beazer's earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C12
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the near-term headwinds are weak affordability, sustained incentives, higher land and financing costs, the integration of Beazer, expected deal abandonment charges in the fourth quarter and the 2027 commitments maturity; the tailwinds are cost reductions already under way, shorter cycle times and a backlog made up mostly of spec homes that close quickly. Over three to five years the main supports are constrained housing supply, which management says remains favorable, and scale benefits if synergies arrive, while the main pressure is the 2028 refinancing cluster and the fixed charges of the preferred stock and assumed notes.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 32; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dfh_dfh-q32026xer-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dfh.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C8; calculation C10
### Downside scenario

The scenario starts with mortgage rates staying high through the fourth quarter, so closings miss the guidance and incentives rise. The first operating break is homebuilding gross margin: a further 3.2 percentage point fall, the same as the fall between the first nine months of 2025 and 2026, takes last-twelve-months EBITDA from USD 373.312 million to USD 247.068 million, lifting net leverage to 7.08x and cutting EBITDA cover of cash interest to 0.81x on pre-closing debt. Financially, operating cash outflow continues while inventory is carried, so borrowing on the Credit Agreement rises toward its borrowing base and liquidity falls below the pre-closing runway of 15.42 months; the Series B dividend of USD 20.25 million a quarter could be deferred, which compounds the claim at 12.0%. Management levers are terminating land options, cutting overhead and slowing starts. On pre-closing figures liquidity would cover about 15.42 months of the outflow, so distress in 2027 is not indicated, but the post-closing position that decides it is not established, and resilience depends on refinancing the August 2028 cluster. The observable triggers are fourth-quarter closings, gross margin, liquidity after closing and any sale of pledged founder shares.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C13
### Overall credit view

Overall, Dream Finders presents an adequate business profile supported by an asset-light land model, regional breadth and integrated financial services, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 4.69x, interest cover of 1.23x, negative free cash flow and compressed margins before a large acquisition. Cash-flow durability appears weak because inventory growth absorbs earnings. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on housing demand and on market access in 2027 and 2028, when USD 300.0 million of commitments and then 60.07% to 75.10% of pre-closing debt mature. The primary downside path is a further fall in homebuilding gross margin on a larger debt and preferred stock base. Further analysis would require the closing balance sheet, the Credit Agreement drawing, covenant definitions and Beazer's earnings. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: refinancing the August 2028 maturities after margin compression and a debt-funded acquisition.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C6; calculation C8; calculation C13
